question: Does body condition add held-out initiation information when non-events must have observed post-release tracking beyond a common time horizon?
source: Pinned PieterjanVerhelst/eel-meta-analysis; same 575 FIII/FIV/FV individuals as V4; fixed nine expert non-migrant overrides; event = canonical downstream onset timestamp, not source terminal positive set
event: first canonical detected behavioral onset >= release and <= release + horizon
nonevent: no onset <= horizon; last recorded receiver arrival >= release + horizon
excluded: no event within horizon and no recorded arrival beyond horizon; this is informative selection, not missing-at-random correction; also exclude the four canonical algorithm-positive eels without a parseable onset timestamp rather than misclassify them as 30-day nonevents
evaluate: at each horizon leave one entire source project out, train a baseline stage+length+release-timing model and an expanded baseline+weight-for-length residual; evaluate AUC on heldout initiator/noninitiator pairs within each project-year only
sample_integrity: No event can be counted after horizon; no nonevent included without observed >=horizon last arrival; all nine expert non-migrants remain nonevents unless last arrival meets horizon. Heldout project outcomes never used to estimate coefficients. Exclude algorithm-positive tracks whose onset timestamp cannot be reconstructed.
output: per-window total included, events, controls, excluded, project/stratum counts, pooled AUC delta, per-project direction; intervals from 10,000 bootstraps of source projects with fit weights fixed, not independent prospective validation
status_rule: An initial 30-day condition increment is transportable only if positive and its project bootstrap CI excludes zero with ≥4 informative projects. Otherwise no demonstrated general condition increment at fixed observation horizon.
boundaries: A last arrival after a horizon documents later detection, not continuous array coverage or full tracking surveillance.
Events are eligible when observed early even if last arrival occurs before horizon; non-events require later detection. The asymmetry can itself induce selection.
Excluding short-observed nonevents is an ascertainment sensitivity, not inverse-probability correction or unbiased migration probability.
Unknown detection probability, mortality and undetected downstream movement remain confounded.
No interpretation of fixed-window noninitiation as biological failure or escapement deficit.
Multiple windows are a frozen sensitivity series; do not select a window after seeing a favorable effect.
